summary.oneLiner: A North-East India tea plantation company producing Assam and Cachar CTC tea and diversifying into Orthodox tea through new factories at its Kanu and Pathemara tea estates.
summary.business: The Grob Tea Company Limited cultivates, manufactures and sells tea from its tea estates in Assam and Cachar, North-East India, producing predominantly CTC tea (Assam CTC and Cachar CTC) with a growing Orthodox tea line, sold into domestic and export markets. The company employs over 3,781 people across its tea estates and other establishments.

The company employs over 3,781 people across its tea estates and other establishments.

- **Orthodox Tea:** Orthodox tea

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- World tea production rose ~2.5% in 2025; India's crop grew ~5%, with growth concentrated in the small tea growers (STG) segment (57% share) while the organized sector's share fell to 43%, a trend management describes as steadily continuing.
- India achieved a record tea export of 280M kgs in 2025 (up 9% YoY); early indications suggest exports may rise further if the geopolitical situation stays favourable, which would strengthen and stabilise the domestic market.
- Import of cheap tea varieties getting mixed with domestic production is flagged as a threat to market stability; improvement in internal (domestic) consumption is seen as a potential offsetting driver.
- Tea crop remains entirely rain-dependent; erratic climate change (longer dry spells punctuated by heavy short rain) is jeopardising production across all tea-growing regions, particularly the North-East.
- Current season (2026) started with drought-like conditions but improved as it progressed; company gardens are running ahead of crop, most notably Doyang and Dessoi (Jorhat & Golaghat district circle, up 64% and 66% respectively), and the market has been steady and buoyant with average price realization up Rs. 45/kg over the previous year.
- FY26 price realization decline (Assam CTC -7.70%, Cachar -1.46%) attributed to supply-demand mechanics of the market rather than company-specific factors.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Diversify into Orthodox tea production (new factories commissioned at Kanu T.E. and under construction at Pathemara T.E.) to explore new markets beyond the core CTC business.
- Ongoing Project Work on Climate Change (PWCC) to mitigate climate-change impact and improve micro-climate around tea gardens, including upgrading irrigation set capacity/efficiency to reduce drought impact.
- Continued drive to improve produce quality through addition/replacement of old machinery and adoption of latest technology in plantation and factory operations.
- Conversion of factory fuel from gas firing to coal firing to structurally lower Power & Fuel cost.
- Declaration of an annual dividend is part of the ordinary business transacted at each AGM (FY26 Notice agenda item: 'To declare a dividend for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026'); no further capital-allocation philosophy (buyback, debt-reduction target, reinvestment policy) is disclosed in this bundle.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company commissioned a new Orthodox tea factory at Kanu T.E., which went into production from July 2025 and produced 2.74 lac kgs of Orthodox tea in FY26. It is now building a second Orthodox tea factory at Pathemara T.E. (Cachar), with capacity to produce 10.00 lac kgs of Orthodox tea annually; construction is ongoing and production is expected to begin by end of August 2026, diversifying the company's product mix and enabling it to explore new markets for Cachar produce.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated operations from tea plantation to processing, ensuring control over quality and supply chain.
- Established presence in Assam's key tea-growing regions (Jorhat and Golaghat) with favorable micro-climates supporting production recovery.
- Long-standing industry experience and stable workforce of over 3,781 employees, with cordial industrial relations.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Climate change / rain-dependent crop — Tea crop is entirely rain-dependent; erratic climate change with very high ambient temperature and erratic rainfall patterns (long dry spells punctuated by heavy short rain) is flagged as frequently jeopardising production across all tea-growing regions, particularly the North-East.
- Labour-intensive operating model — Tea being a labour-intensive industry, shortage of labour during peak season plus a substantial increase in labour, social and other input costs is flagged as the major structural cause of concern for the industry.
- Tea price realization volatility — Average sale price realization fell across Assam CTC (-7.70%), Cachar and Orthodox varieties in FY26 due to the supply-demand mechanism of the market, directly driving the fall in the Company's profitability during the year.
- Cheap tea imports diluting the domestic market — Import of cheap varieties of tea getting mixed with domestic production is flagged by management as a matter of serious concern for market stability.
- Mid-cycle statutory auditor transition — Incumbent statutory auditor M/s GARV & Associates resigned effective 13th May, 2026, immediately after issuing the FY26 audit report; M/s B Nath & Company was appointed to fill the casual vacancy, subject to shareholder ratification/approval at the ensuing AGM.
- Secretarial-audit compliance observations (prior year) — The FY2024-25 secretarial audit flagged incomplete/delayed disclosure to stock exchanges around a Company Secretary's resignation, and a non-compliance under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulation 9 concerning disclosure by an immediate relative of a designated person; remedial clarifications/responses were filed with the exchanges.
